newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gulf War reparations fund gets cash from oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Gulf War reparations fund gets cash from oil deal.

text.p: The Gulf War reparations fund has received its first cash from the oil-for-food deal and should be able to pay $142 million in individual claims against Iraq at the end of February, the United Nations said on Thursday.

The U.N. Compensation Commission, set up by the Security Council in 1991 to assess damages caused by Iraq's invasion and seven-month occupation of Kuwait, is to get 30 per cent of revenues from the limited oil sales, or $100 million monthly.
Carlos Alzamora, executive secretary, said in a statement that the Geneva-based fund had received $20 million on Thursday following implementation of Security Council resolution 986.

The long-delayed deal, signed last May but authorised in December, enables Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods to help offset the effects of sanctions.

At the current pace of incoming weekly revenue, a first group of 57,000 successful individual claimants from 63 countries will each be paid an initial $2,500 as early as the end of February, according to the statement.
"The total amount of compensation to be paid to this group at this stage amounts to $142 million," Alzamora said.
This first batch of claimants are people forced to depart Kuwait or Iraq due to the invasion as well as individuals claiming losses up to $100,000.
To date, the Geneva-based fund has only been able to pay out $13.5 million to nearly 4,000 priority claimants who suffered serious personal injury or the death of a close relative.

In all, it has received 2.6 million claims worth $220 billion from individuals, firms and governments for losses allegedly caused by Iraq. Its funding has been precarious, but has been boosted with the implementation of the oil deal.
